title: a native pin whose graph reaches a host module through `export * from` fails to compile, and the diagnostic names the laundering module
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH, so a requirement reached through another module is the same requirement, and 'The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the JavaScript-host dependence that page names, and `blocksNativePin` refuses `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. `messageContains` pins the route because a pin refused with an empty route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly. The SMITHERS1510 companion lands in the auxiliary module, at the edge that reaches `node:fs`, because a re-export runs the target module's initializer exactly as an import does; it is declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md). This is the spelling with no alias to follow: `checker.getImmediateAliasedSymbol` returns undefined for `export * from "node:fs"` because no `node:` module resolves inside the analyzer's virtual project, which is precisely the hostile case. It is a separate case from the named re-export because a fix that only followed checker aliases would pass that one and fail this one. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to accept this program, grant the pin and print `9` — zero diagnostics where the reference reports SMITHERS1510@4:15 in star-reexport-host-module.mod.sm and SMITHERS3001@16:1 in the case. This is the spelling with no checker alias to follow, and the fork's walk now has a syntax fallback for `export * from` for exactly that reason (`nativeLaunderWalk`, compiler/forkbridge/nativepin.go.txt). It satisfies the declared route `-> star-reexport-host-module.mod.sm -> node:fs`; measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
